runbooks.diagnosis: Let's Encrypt rate limits hit — usually after repeated re-creation of the traefik container with a lost acme.json or a wildcard/san burst. The LE staging/duplicate limit is 5 failures per hour, 50 certs per week per domain.
remediation: Stop recreating the traefik container; preserve the acme.json volume across restarts
Verify the requested domains (duplicate certificate limit is 5/week)
Wait out the rate-limit window (1h for validations, 7d for certificates)
Switch to the LE staging endpoint while debugging issuance

runbooks.diagnosis: Traefik did not pick up the dynamic config or the target container has no matching router labels/network attachment. Most common in this stack: service is on a different compose network than traefik, or the router rule host mismatches the requested domain.
remediation: Confirm the service shares the traefik network (opensme-net)
Compare the router rule host with the actual request Host header
Check traefik logs for 'router ... error' lines naming the service
Restart traefik only after config verification

runbooks.diagnosis: acme.json must be 0600; Docker volume copies can reset permissions and traefik refuses to start with a world-readable acme file.
remediation: chmod 600 the acme.json inside the traefik-data volume

runbooks.diagnosis: The base compose's portal-web router (priority 100, backend :3000 — the Next app NOT running under the demo profile) shadowed the demo profile's portal-https router (default rule-length priority ~32): every portal request, including the https bounce, answered 502 against the dead :3000 backend.
remediation: Verify the https router wins over portal-web on :443

runbooks.diagnosis: The fleet Traefik's docker-provider event stream dies after docker-daemon restarts on this OpenVZ host; the file-provider standin routers pin hardcoded backend IPs (portal-standin→.21:8080, webmail-standin→.7:3000, mail-home-standin→.22:8080) that a restart reshuffled (portal moved to .5, stalwart to .18) — stale pins 502.
remediation: Refresh the standin IP=port pins after any docker-daemon restart (roles refresh after deploy)
Prefer service-name DNS over hardcoded IPs where possible
Verify each standin router against the current container IP before relying on it

runbooks.diagnosis: The calendar/calendar-dav/vc-room routers kept certresolver=letsencrypt from the built-in traefik; under profiles/system-traefik.yml that resolver does not exist, so the routes 404. The fix attaches them to traefik-web and re-points the three routers at the mytlschallenge resolver (calendar-radicale keeps its pinned static address).
remediation: Apply the router overrides: attach calendar/calendar-dav/vc-room to traefik-web with certresolver=mytlschallenge
Verify the calendar and vc-room routes answer on https
